fixes.explanation: I get why a morning offering sounds right, friend. It sounds like something a good baker would do before the oven's even warm. But it's not in these verses. God opens with “You shall have no other gods before Me.” (Exodus 20:3). Before anything else, He wants to be the only God on the list.

A king is a big thing to want, friend, but this command isn't about thrones. God says, “You shall not make for yourself an idol in the form of anything in the heavens above, on the earth below, or in the waters beneath.” (Exodus 20:4). Sky, land and sea, and not one of them gets carved into a god. I once stood in a junk drawer so long I almost started worshiping a rubber band, and even that wouldn't have been allowed.

You've got it, baker! God says, “for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God…” (Exodus 20:5). He says it right after telling them not to bow down to idols or worship them. He doesn't want to share the spot. Nice and clean, just like a good stamp.

Not quite, friend. The text says, “…they trembled and stood at a distance.” (Exodus 20:18). Thunder, lightning, a ram's horn and a mountain wrapped in smoke, and the people back up. They don't run closer. If my kitchen did all that, I'd be standing way back by the door too. So the answer is False.
